The Underlying is the 12-month percentage change in the U.S. All-Property Commercial Property Price Index reported by Green Street for October 2027, comparing October 2027 with October 2026.

markets.rules_primary: If legislation dedicating more sales tax revenue to mass transit is enacted in Pennsylvania before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Enactment requires completion of all constitutional and legal requirements for the legislation to become binding law.

Standard legislation requiring executive approval: final passage by all required legislative bodies, executive signature OR becoming law despite executive inaction OR successful veto override, and satisfaction of any required waiting periods
Legislation not requiring executive approval: final passage and completion of required waiting periods
Constitutional amendments: passage with required supermajorities and completion of ratification processes
Executive orders: official signature, publication in official government records, and legal effectiveness

The following do NOT constitute enactment:

Legislative passage without completed executive action
Passage by only some required bodies
Provisional passage
Non-binding resolutions
Draft orders

Enactment occurs when all requirements are completed, regardless of pending judicial challenges.

For this market, dedicating more sales tax revenue to mass transit means a Pennsylvania law that newly dedicates, or increases, a recurring (annual or ongoing) transfer of state sales and use tax revenue to the Public Transportation Trust Fund or another fund used for public transportation, whether the transfer is set as a percentage of that revenue or as a dollar amount. An increase to an existing transfer, including the transfer under 74 Pa.C.S. 1506(b)(3.4), counts, and so does an increase in the state sales and use tax rate whose added revenue is dedicated to public transportation. It may be a stand-alone bill or part of a budget or other bill, and the increase may be phased in over time. The effective date of the law is not relevant; only that it has been enacted.

Continuing the existing sales tax transfers without increasing them does NOT count. A one-time appropriation or transfer, a General Fund appropriation, a tax or fee other than the state sales and use tax, and an administrative transfer of capital funds do NOT count. Executive orders, agency actions and local ordinances do NOT count.

Constitutional amendments: passage with required supermajorities and completion of ratification processes
Executive orders: official signature, publication in official government records, and legal effectiveness

The following do NOT constitute enactment:

Legislative passage without completed executive action
Passage by only some required bodies
Provisional passage
Non-binding resolutions
Draft orders

Enactment occurs when all requirements are completed, regardless of pending judicial challenges.

For this market, dedicating more sales tax revenue to mass transit means a Pennsylvania law that newly dedicates, or increases, a recurring (annual or ongoing) transfer of state sales and use tax revenue to the Public Transportation Trust Fund or another fund used for public transportation, whether the transfer is set as a percentage of that revenue or as a dollar amount. An increase to an existing transfer, including the transfer under 74 Pa.C.S. 1506(b)(3.4), counts, and so does an increase in the state sales and use tax rate whose added revenue is dedicated to public transportation. It may be a stand-alone bill or part of a budget or other bill, and the increase may be phased in over time. The effective date of the law is not relevant; only that it has been enacted.

Continuing the existing sales tax transfers without increasing them does NOT count. A one-time appropriation or transfer, a General Fund appropriation, a tax or fee other than the state sales and use tax, and an administrative transfer of capital funds do NOT count. Executive orders, agency actions and local ordinances do NOT count.
